events.title: Anthropic Claude Opus 4.6 released
events.summary: [Anthropic] released Claude Opus 4.6 on February 5, 2026 — stronger agentic coding, 1M-token context, and state-of-the-art terminal and knowledge-work benchmarks.
events.about: Opus 4.6 added adaptive thinking, agent teams in Claude Code, and Excel and PowerPoint integrations for knowledge work. It led Terminal-Bench 2.0 and Humanity's Last Exam — [Anthropic]'s answer to GPT-5.2 and [Gemini] 3 Pro in the agentic coding arms race.

narrative.whyChosen: Opus 4.6 made million-token agentic coding a production [Anthropic] tier.
narrative.whyImportant: Parallel agent teams and adaptive thinking pushed multi-hour autonomous work mainstream.
narrative.problemSolved: Enterprise coding agents needed better long-context retrieval and sustained focus on large codebases.

events.title: OpenAI GPT-5.3-Codex released
events.summary: OpenAI released GPT-5.3-Codex on February 5, 2026 — an agentic coding model merging Codex performance with GPT-5.2 reasoning, 25% faster in Codex tools.
events.about: GPT-5.3-Codex handled long-running research, tool use, and complex execution while staying steerable mid-task — OpenAI's answer to Claude Opus 4.6 in the same week. OpenAI said early versions helped build the model itself, and it shipped in Codex app, [CLI], and IDE extensions on GB200 systems.

narrative.whyChosen: GPT-5.3-Codex unified OpenAI's coding and reasoning stacks in one agentic model.
narrative.whyImportant: Interactive steering during long agent runs became a baseline Codex feature.
narrative.problemSolved: Developers juggled separate Codex and GPT models for coding versus general reasoning.
